questions.question: When exactly is the `__init__` method executed?
options: Only when you manually call it using `object.__init__()`.
Automatically, immediately after a new object is created.
Every time you change an attribute's value.
Only when the program finishes running.
questions.explanation: The `__init__` method is a constructor; Python triggers it automatically the moment you instantiate a class to set up the new object.

questions.question: In the line `self.color = color`, what is the purpose of `self`?
options: It is a keyword that makes the variable global.
It refers to the Class blueprint rather than the individual object.
It represents the specific instance of the object being created or modified.
It is a required name for the color of the object.
questions.explanation: `self` is a reference to the specific instance. It allows Python to keep track of which object's data it is currently updating.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes an 'Instance Attribute'?
options: A variable shared by every single object of a class.
A variable that can only be used once in the entire program.
Data that is unique to a specific object, usually defined inside `__init__`.
A special method that starts with double underscores.
questions.explanation: Instance attributes are tied to a specific object via `self`. This is why one Car object can have the make 'Toyota' while another has 'Lada'.
